_comment: Committed safe-defaults that travel with the repo. Per-machine extras (HW_TEST=1 commands tied to local hardware, blanket Bash(*), domain restrictions for sensitive sites) belong in settings.local.json which is not committed. Patterns here are: read-only inspection, in-tree builds, QEMU unit tests, and WebFetch for documentation domains relevant to the project (Pi datasheets, RFCs, ARM docs). Anything that could mutate remote state (git push/reset/force, rm -rf, etc.) is intentionally NOT committed — those need explicit per-session approval or per-machine local opt-in. Trust assumptions worth knowing: Bash(make:*) trusts whatever recipe lives in Makefile, so checking out an untrusted branch and running make would auto-execute that branch's targets — review Makefile diffs in PRs accordingly. Bash(find:*) does not narrow against -exec/-delete, so the same trust assumption applies to find invocations from session prompts. Both are deliberate tradeoffs: the alternative is constant permission prompts on routine commands, which trains the user to click-through.
